[Figure 1](attached-image-1)

A rectangle intersects a circle as shown: \(AB=4,\) \(BC=5\) and \(DE=3.\) Then \(EF\) equals

[Figure 1](attached-image-2)

Figure \(ABCD\) is a trapezoid with \(AB\parallel DC,\) \(AB=5,\) \(BC=3\sqrt2,\) \(\angle BCD=45^\circ\) and \(\angle CDA=60^\circ.\) The length of \(DC\) is

[Figure 1](attached-image-3)

A right triangle \(ABC\) with hypotenuse \(AB\) has side \(AC=15.\) Altitude \(CH\) divides \(AB\) into segments \(AH\) and \(HB,\) with \(HB=16.\) The area of \(\triangle ABC\) is

[Figure 1](attached-image-4)

In the obtuse triangle \(ABC,\) \(AM=MB,\) \(MD\perp BC,\) \(EC\perp BC.\) If the area of \(\triangle ABC\) is \(24,\) then the area of \(\triangle BED\) is

[Figure 1](attached-image-5)

In \(\triangle ABC,\) \(D\) is on \(AC\) and \(F\) is on \(BC.\) Also, \(AB\perp AC,\) \(AF\perp BC,\) and \(BD=DC=FC=1.\) Find \(AC.\)

[Figure 1](attached-image-6)

In an arcade game, the “monster” is the shaded sector of a circle of radius \(1\) cm, as shown in the figure. The missing piece (the mouth) has central angle \(60^\circ.\) What is the perimeter of the monster in cm?

[Figure 1](attached-image-7)

In right \(\triangle ABC\) with legs \(5\) and \(12,\) arcs of circles are drawn, one with center \(A\) and radius \(12,\) the other with center \(B\) and radius \(5.\) They intersect the hypotenuse in \(M\) and \(N.\) Then \(MN\) has length
